# Elements

Elements is a component framework for building application UI with LLMs and humans working together.

Primary docs:
- Overview: /elements
- AI builder guide: /elements/ai
- Theming: /elements/theming
- Component spec: /elements/component-spec
- Studio: /elements/components/studio
- Blocks: /elements/blocks/dashboard
- Components: /elements/components/button
- Headless web components: /elements/headless

Philosophy:
- Prefer composition over invention.
- Use Elements primitives for behaviour and accessibility.
- Use visual primitives for surfaces and layout polish.
- Use blocks for complete app screens and common product patterns.
- Keep generated UI editable in Studio.
- Use token-based theming names such as bg-background, text-foreground, bg-card, text-card-foreground, bg-popover, text-popover-foreground, bg-primary, text-primary-foreground, bg-secondary, text-secondary-foreground, text-muted-foreground, border-border, border-input, ring-ring, bg-success, bg-warning, and bg-destructive.
- Do not use raw colours unless defining a theme.
- Prefer component props for behaviour and classes for layout, spacing, and small visual adjustments.
- Give generated nodes stable ids and human labels when returning Studio specs.
- Components are discovered from src/pages/elements/components/*/El*.vue, src/pages/elements/forms/*/El*.vue, and src/pages/elements/visual/*/El*.vue.
- Component metadata currently lives in defineOptions({ __doc: ... }). Studio-specific decoration can live in __doc.studio or __studio.
- Prop inspector metadata currently lives on prop definitions as _edit. Prefer _edit.component over the legacy _edit.editor alias.

Current component families:
- Behaviour components: Button, Dropdown, Dialog, Drawer, Tabs, Toggle, Tooltip, Accordion, Menu, Listbox, Combobox, Autocomplete, Popover, Toast, Command palette.
- Form components: Field, Checkbox, Radio group, Text input, Password input, Calendar, Textarea, Code input, JSON input, JSON list input, Number input, Select input, Native select, Boolean input, Color input.
- Visual components: Card.
- Blocks: Dashboard, Chat, Mail, Forms, Login, Application layout.

LLM generation rules:
1. Choose an existing block when the request matches a known app pattern.
2. Choose existing components before writing custom HTML.
3. Keep accessibility inside components; do not recreate keyboard navigation by hand.
4. Prefer native form behaviour where it is useful, especially on mobile.
5. Use Field to wrap custom controls that need consistent labels, required markers, and descriptions.
6. Use Code input for prompts, templates, snippets, and structured text that benefits from a code editor.
7. Use JSON input for editable schemas, tool payloads, app config, and other parsed structured data.
8. Use JSON list input for schema-aware arrays of objects, especially inspector editors for menu items, commands, options, toasts, and people lists.
9. Return an editable Studio spec when the user may want to inspect or revise the UI later.
10. Use clear layer labels and stable ids in specs.
11. Do not invent new theme colour names; use the theme page token names.
12. Keep generated interfaces dense, practical, and product-like unless the user asks for a marketing page.

Component discovery and documentation:
- To add a component, create a folder under /elements/components, /elements/forms, or /elements/visual and add an El*.vue component file.
- Add an Index.vue beside the component for bespoke documentation. If no Index.vue exists, the docs route is generated from the inspected component metadata and runtime props.
- Use __doc.name, __doc.tag, __doc.description, __doc.icon, __doc.events, and __doc.slots to make generated docs useful.
- Use __doc.hidden or __doc.nav.hidden to hide helper components from generated navigation.
- Use __doc.studio.hidden to hide helper components from the Studio palette while keeping them available to code.
- Use __doc.icon for the canonical SVG path icon. Sidebar fallback icons are presentation-only.
- The component row is discovery data: id, path, section, slug, exportName, route, and component or loader.
- The inspected component row decorates that with __doc, studio metadata, props, label, badge, icon, order, hidden flags, navHidden, and studioHidden.
- Studio renderer specs are UI trees with id, label, component, props, and children. They are different from component discovery rows.

Future AI-specific areas:
- AI chat tools that return editable UI.
- Voice tools and multimodal controls.
- Agent task runners that stream status into UI.
- Server-backed autocomplete and search patterns.
- Tool-call result renderers.
